description: Anterior branch of the radial vein; bears dark spinules and hairs in Simulium, while presence or absence of spiniform setae on the distal R1 vein separates subgenera of Austrosimulium (Dumbleton 1963; Takaoka et al. 2016; Srisuka et al. 2024).
Posterior branch of the cubital vein; straight or gently curved in Cnephia and Gigantodax versus double-curved in Simulium and Austrosimulium (Dumbleton 1963).
First pair of legs (coxa, trochanter, femur, tibia and tarsus); fore basitarsus width and dorsal hair crest are diagnostic in females and males (Takaoka et al. 2016; Srisuka et al. 2024).
Second pair of legs; colour patterns of mid coxa, femur, tibia and basitarsus are used in adult keys (Takaoka et al. 2016; Srisuka et al. 2024).
Third pair of legs; bears the parallel-sided or spindle-shaped hind basitarsus with calcipala and the second tarsomere with pedisulcus (Takaoka et al. 2016; Srisuka et al. 2024).
Paired sensory hairs (unbranched or branched) on each side of the pupal frons (Takaoka et al. 2016; Srisuka et al. 2024).
Sensory hair on each side of the pupal face, compared in length with the frontal trichomes (Takaoka et al. 2016; Srisuka et al. 2024).
Sensory hairs on the pupal thorax (anterodorsal, anterolateral, mediolateral and ventrolateral); branching and length aid pupal identification (Takaoka et al. 2016; Srisuka et al. 2024).
Row of minute hair-like projections along the posterior margin of each primary (main) ray of the larval labral fan (Srisuka et al. 2024).
Row of long colourless sensilla just posterior to the basal juncture of the larval anal sclerite, anterior to the posterior circlet (Srisuka et al. 2024).
Whole body of the mature (final-instar) larva in dorsal and lateral views, showing abdominal pigmentation pattern and the darkened thoracic gill histoblast laterally (Srisuka et al. 2024).
